traits.leader.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 612): 'a short crooked trunk ... stout spreading branches ... forming a low wide head'.

traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.48, 0.56, 0.3], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Parkinsonia microphylla (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.62 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.62, branches 0.59. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a small, much-branched tree 3 to 6 m tall, its yellow-green bark doing most of the photosynthesis, its twigs ending in thorns, with tiny pinnate leaves dropped in drought and pale yellow flowers in spring. Not fitted to measurements. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius. Its crown's base is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured share of the tree's height below its crown (crown_base_share, USDA Urban Tree Database), and its stem divides only where its flora or photographs say its leader is lost or that it stands on several stems, since 2026-10-24, in place of hand-set crown_base and fork values.

generator.params.bud_years.note: Short shoots leaf out for up to 40 years while they have light, fitted with the seed plants' shoot spacing so that leaf area per crown area rises with age as the Urban Tree Database's city trees of Parkinsonia (P. aculeata and P. florida, Glendale, Arizona) does, rather than falling once the crown has filled.

generator.params.spur_leaf.note: A short shoot's leaf card draws a cluster of its small leaves, a branchlet's worth, 0.2 m long, so that the crown keeps within the module limit; the seed plants' rules space the shoots from the card's area.

generator.params.spur_pairs.note: Two pairs of leaves a year on each short shoot, a sparser crown than the Urban Tree Database's irrigated blue and Mexican palo verdes (Parkinsonia florida and P. aculeata, 1.6 to 1.8 leaf per crown area at 10 to 25 years): the foothill palo verde does most of its photosynthesis in its green bark and drops its tiny leaves in drought, so its branches show through.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 3 m at 20 years and 5 m at 60. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: yellow-green bark and twigs, sparse grey-green leaflets, pale yellow flowers. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth yellow-green bark that photosynthesises; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five pale yellow petals between five sepals, ten stamens and one pistil, from the characters of Fabaceae and Parkinsonia by the rules at the flowering plants.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: The Desert Legume Program's account of the palo verdes, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): leaves of one pair of pinnae with 4 to 8 pairs of leaflets each, the smallest leaflets of the palo verdes. Isley's monograph (1975, as the New York Botanical Garden's copy is quoted) gives (2) 3 to 5 (9) pairs, sessile and ovate, 1 to 2 mm long. Even-pinnate.

appearance.organs.leaf.note: The leaf drawn as a twice-divided compound leaf (spec rework P4): its one pair of pinnae and their leaflets counted from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants; before, a fern's frond stood in for it. By eye from photographs: the pinnae forking narrowly, about 22 degrees either side; the leaflets ovate and blunt, about 0.6 as wide as long.

traits.thorn_position.note: Abrams (vol. 2, 1944, p. 479), as Cercidium microphyllum: branchlets spine-tipped but without side spines, so its thorns tip its twigs and none stand beside its buds.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams (vol. 2, 1944, p. 479), as Cercidium microphyllum: shrubby or small tree 2-8 m high with smooth light grey-green bark; branchlets spine-tipped but without side spines; leaves with no common rachis, the two stalkless pinnae 1-3 cm long; leaflets 4-8 pairs, elliptic, 1-2 mm long; pedicels 5-15 mm; petals yellow, 5-7 mm long; pods 4-6 cm, hardly flattened, 1-4-seeded, much constricted between the seeds, with a long pointed beak; March to May. Genus (p. 479): flowers in short corymb-like clusters; petals 5, yellow; stamens 10.

traits.height_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 426), as Cercidium microphyllum: genus to about 8 m, young bark smooth and green, flowers in corymb-like clusters, leafless in the dry season; the species with yellowish-green young bark, the common rachis nearly absent so leaves look once-pinnate, leaflets 4-8 pairs per pinna, not over 3 mm, flowers pale yellow with the odd (upper) petal often whitish, pod swollen ending in a flat beak; ends of the leafy branchlets spine-tipped; April to May.
